2608.05075.title: German parties shifted towards intuition-based rhetoric after the far right's parliamentary breakthrough
2608.05075.paper_summary: The spread of misinformation is widely perceived as a threat to democratic deliberation, yet how political elites' rhetorical commitments to truth shift alongside the rise of populist actors remains poorly understood. Analysing 4.5 million tweets and 59,170 parliamentary speeches by German political elites between 2015 and 2025, we measure evidence-based and intuition-based rhetoric using a validated distributed dictionary representation. Across both arenas, intuition-based language has become more prominent, and right-leaning actors consistently exhibit the lowest Evidence Minus Intuition (EMI) scores. The parliamentary entry of the extreme-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) in 2017 coincides with sharp downward shifts in EMI across the broader chamber, while a more gradual decline is observed on Twitter. These findings document an association between far-right visibility and a changing approach to truth in elite discourse in a multiparty European democracy.
2608.05075.paper_summary_zh: 假資訊的擴散被廣泛視為對民主辯論的威脅，但政治精英對真相的修辭承諾如何隨著民粹主義者的興起而變化，仍然不甚了解。通過分析2015年至2025年間德國政治精英的450萬條推文和59,170篇議會演講，我們使用經過驗證的分佈式字典表示法來衡量基於證據和基於直覺的修辭。在這兩個領域中，基於直覺的語言變得更加突出，而右派參與者始終表現出最低的證據減去直覺（EMI）得分。極右派德國另類選擇黨（AfD）在2017年進入議會，恰逢整個議會EMI出現急劇下降，而在推特上則觀察到更為緩慢的下降。這些發現記錄了極右派的可見性與多黨制歐洲民主中精英話語中對真相的變化方法之間的關聯。
2608.05075.author: Peer Saleth et.al.
2608.05075.authors: Peer Saleth, Segun T. Aroyehun, Fabio Carrella, Christoph M. Abels, Stephan Lewandowsky, David Garcia
